html: Cells meet electrophiles and peroxides with one inducible programme. At rest the KEAP1-CUL3-RBX1 ubiquitin ligase binds the transcription factor NRF2 at two motifs and marks it for the proteasome, so NRF2 is made continuously and lives under twenty minutes. Stress does not pull the two apart: it modifies the sensor cysteines of KEAP1 - an adduct from an electrophile such as 4-hydroxynonenal or a particle-derived quinone, a disulfide between Cys226, Cys613, Cys622 and Cys624 from hydrogen peroxide - and the loaded ligase stops working, so newly made NRF2 escapes into the nucleus. There it pairs with a small MAF protein, and only that heterodimer binds the antioxidant response element. The programme it drives is both the defence and its own brake: glutamate-cysteine ligase and glutathione synthetase refill glutathione, which lets glutathione peroxidase clear the peroxide and glutathione S-transferase A4 conjugate the aldehyde that started it; heme oxygenase 1 opens heme to biliverdin and ferrous iron; and NRF2 also drives the genes of KEAP1 itself and of BACH1, the repressor that competes for the same enhancers and arrives late, which is what makes heme oxygenase induction transient. Heme lifts that repression by binding BACH1 directly. One arm in this module runs the other way: NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase 1 reduces the o-quinones of combustion particles by two electrons to a catechol that is unstable in air and oxidises straight back, releasing superoxide, so for these substrates the step amplifies redox cycling instead of ending it.
